served.stem: (S)-2-phenylpropanamide is treated with LiAlH4, then aqueous workup. The stereocenter is at the carbon alpha to the carbonyl. What is the major organic product, including correct configuration?
served.bankWhy: LiAlH4 reduces the amide to a primary amine (C=O becomes CH2, nitrogen retained), giving 2-phenylpropan-1-amine. Distractor 1 inverts the center (R), the alcohol comes from wrongly treating the amide like an acid, the aldehyde is an incorrect reduction, and the last option adds a ring methyl.

answer.line: LiAlH4 turns the amide C=O into CH2 and keeps the nitrogen. No bond to the stereocenter breaks, so it stays S.

steps: Name what LiAlH4 does to a primary amide: C(=O)NH2 becomes CH2NH2. The oxygen leaves; the nitrogen stays.
Check the stereocenter. None of its four bonds breaks, so every group keeps its place, wedges and dashes included.
Check the label. CH2NH2 and phenyl tie at the first atom, a C each, so look one atom out: N, H, H beats C, C, C, and the order holds: still S.

choices.note: C=O out, nitrogen kept, stereocenter untouched: still S.
This is the mirror image, the enantiomer. Nothing in the reaction touches the stereocenter, so nothing inverts.

choices.display: the amine with an extra methyl on the ring
choices.note: This adds a methyl to the ring. No reagent here brings a carbon.
An aldehyde is a partial reduction, what DIBAL-H gives from an ester or a nitrile. LiAlH4 on an amide goes all the way to the amine.
LiAlH4 on an ester or an acid gives a primary alcohol. An amide keeps its nitrogen and gives an amine.

student.lockIt: LiAlH4 reduces an amide to an amine: C=O becomes CH2, the nitrogen stays, and nearby stereocenters stay.
